title: Why Octopuses Have Three Hearts
description:
Two hearts pump blood through the gills and one through the body. Sources are listed below.

[1] Smithsonian Ocean: https://ocean.si.edu/ocean-life/invertebrates/octopuses
[2] Britannica: https://www.britannica.com/animal/octopus-mollusk

script.show: Slow pan across an octopus on a reef

script.say: Two of them push blood through the gills, and the third sends it around the body. [1]
script.show: Simple diagram of the three hearts

script.say: Its blood is blue because it carries oxygen with a copper-based protein called hemocyanin. [2]
script.show: Blue liquid in a glass, then the octopus again

script.say: When an octopus swims, the body heart stops beating, which is one reason they prefer to crawl. [1]
script.show: Octopus crawling along the sea floor

script.say: So next time you see one walking across the rocks, it may simply be saving its heart.
